name: Type A
description: An ungrounded plug with two flat parallel blades, widely associated with North America and Japan.

name: Type B
description: A grounded North American plug with two flat blades and a round or U-shaped earth pin.

name: Type C
description: The two-round-pin Europlug is ungrounded and commonly used for lower-power devices across many regions.

name: Type D
description: A grounded three-round-pin plug arranged in a triangle and used primarily in India and Nepal.

name: Type E
description: A grounded European system with two round pins and a contact for the socket's projecting earth pin.

name: Type F
description: The grounded Schuko system uses two round pins and earthing clips on the sides of the plug and socket.

name: Type G
description: A fused, grounded plug with three rectangular pins, used in the United Kingdom and several other countries.

name: Type H
description: The grounded Type H system uses round pins in its modern form and has a distinctive three-pin arrangement.

name: Type I
description: A plug with two angled flat power pins and, on grounded versions, a vertical earth pin.

name: Type J
description: Switzerland's compact grounded plug has three round pins, with the earth pin offset from the centre line.

name: Type K
description: Denmark's grounded system has two round power pins and a dedicated earth connection below them.

name: Type L
description: Italy's grounded plug has three round pins in a straight line and comes in 10 A and 16 A variants.

name: Type M
description: A large grounded three-round-pin plug based on BS 546 and used for higher-current connections.

name: Type N
description: A modern grounded three-round-pin system used in Brazil and increasingly adopted in South Africa.

name: Type O
description: Thailand's grounded three-round-pin standard is designed for the country's 230 V domestic supply.
